message.content: The existing test on disk expects `"\\r\\n"` for `export_csv([], [])`. My current implementation returns `"\\r\\n\\r\\n"` because it always appends the header plus a trailing CRLF. The expected behavior: header line, then one record per row. The fix: the empty-columns case with empty rows should produce a single `\\r\\n` (the header). My implementation produces `"\\r\\n" + "\\r\\n" = "\\r\\n\\r\\n"`. Wait — my implementation returns `"\\r\\n".join(lines) + "\\r\\n"`. With lines = ["", ""], that's `"\\r\\n" + "\\r\\n"` = `"\\r\\n\\r\\n"`. The test wants `"\\r\\n"` for empty rows. For one row with empty columns, test wants `"\\r\\n\\r\\n"` (header + one empty record). So the logic should be: output = header + CRLF, then each row is a (possibly empty) record followed by CRLF. With empty columns and no rows, output is just header + CRLF = `"\\r\\n"`. That's exactly what my implementation produces if lines = [""] and join gives `"" + "\\r\\n"` = `"\\r\\n"`. My bug: I built lines = [header] and then join + trailing CRLF. With no rows, lines=[""], join([""]) = "", + "\\r\\n" = "\\r\\n". That's correct! But the test failure showed `'\\r\\n\\r\\n'`. That means lines had two elements... Oh wait, the failure was from a different test file version. The test file I just read now says `export_csv([], []) == "\\r\\n"` — my implementation gives exactly that. The earlier failing test was the older version of test_export.py. The file has changed. Let me just re-run the tests.
